item.title: Fixing 'conda: command not found' After Anaconda Installation
item.description:
“Fixing ‘conda: command not found’ After Anaconda Installation”

When setting up a new environment with Anaconda or Miniconda, receiving the error -bash: conda: command not found (or similar on other shells) indicates that the installation directory for the conda executable is not correctly included in your system’s PATH environment variable. This prevents the shell from locating and executing the command.

How can one reliably configure the system’s PATH to make conda accessible from the terminal across various operating systems and shell configurations?

item.title: Solved: How to Fix 'Conda' Not Recognized as an Internal or External Command
item.description:
When trying to utilize conda commands after installing Anaconda on your Windows 7 Professional system, you may come across an error stating that 'conda' is not recognized as an internal or external command. This can be quite frustrating, especially when you believe everything was set up correctly. Below, I will delve into multiple solutions to resolve this issue and ensure smooth functionality of your Anaconda environment.

Potential Resolutions to the ‘Conda’ Command Not Found Error

Insight into the Issue

Upon installation of Anaconda 4.4, a notable change was introduced: the installer no longer modifies the PATH environment variable by default. This can lead to the conda command being unrecognized. It’s recommended to use either the Anaconda Navigator or Anaconda Command Prompt for managing your Anaconda packages. However, you do have some alternatives to manually address the PATH variable.

item.title: Solved: How to Fix Zsh CondaPip Command Not Found Error
item.description:
So you’ve installed Anaconda, and everything seemed to go well until you switched to oh-my-zsh. Suddenly, you’re met with the frustrating message:

zsh: command not found: conda

This issue typically arises when Zsh cannot find the conda command, which can be due to several reasons related to the path and environment variable settings. If you’re looking for a solution to effectively fix this error, here’s a comprehensive guide that outlines multiple methods to resolve the problem and ensure that both conda and pip commands function smoothly in your Zsh environment.
